newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares post 0.96 percent gain, await Chirac.
newsitem.headline: French shares post 0.96 percent gain, await Chirac.

text.p: French shares closed just below their day's high on Tuesday but with a big gain after Monday's four percent fall on a shock election gain for the left.
A softer Wall Street, depressed by stronger than expected May U.S. consumer confidence, did not derail the French advance.

Investors are awaiting a televised address from President Jacques Chirac at 1800 GMT after Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he would not return to office even if the centre-right won the second round of the parliamentary election on Sunday.
The CAC-40 index closed up 25.6 points, or 0.96 percent, at 2,680.34. Of the CAC-40 stocks, 27 closed higher, 13 fell.
The market had started with a 0.72 percent decline as traders braced themselves for a second sell-off as British-based investors returned from a public holiday.
But the sell-off was limited and the market rebounded even before it had fallen to a strong support level at 2,640.

In the afternoon, shares briefly sagged from their higher levels on fears U.S. investors would start selling as they too came back from a holiday. "The surprise is that U.S. investors have not sold. They are still betting on a centre-right victory on Sunday," a broker said.
Opinion is mixed on the market's direction on Wednesday with some brokers seeing the CAC-40 down to 2,600 in the rest of the week while others say it will depend on the Chirac speech and Wall Street.
"He has got to be careful about what he says and avoid turning the election into a vote of confidence," a broker at a British house in Paris said.

"The announcement of (Alain Juppe's) departure, that some had hoped for sooner, could help the right in the second round. We hope that Jacques Chirac states clearly tonight what he expects from his majority," another trader said.

"The departure of Alain Juppe is good news but the impact on the Bourse is very limited. We are awaiting the speech by Jacques Chirac. If he remains vague then the victory of the centre-right can be difficult," another trader said.

"It is not the resignation by Juppe which will determine the result of the second round. The right has sufferend a serious setback and the market remains persuaded that if the left wins there could be a 300 points fall in the CAC," a broker said.
Traders said they would like Chirac to indicate that politicians close to former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur would be included in the new government team.
"The appointment of a Balladur ally such as Nicolas Sarkozy or Francois Leotard as Prime Minister would be very well received in the market," a trader said.

Investors are also keen to see Thursday's National Front decision on what to tell its voters to do in constituencies where it has not reached the second round. Traditionally the Front is of the Right, but Jean-Marie Le Pen recently suggested he may favour boosting the Left in order to hurt Chirac.
Bank Credit Lyonnais was the biggest riser, up 7.66 percent to 229 francs. It fell sharply on Monday with other privatisation stocks.
Dassault Electronique, set to merge with Thomson-CSF if the government selects the Alactel bid over Lagardere, was up 5.10 percent at 371 francs.
